newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Liberia's Taylor stops campaign, poll date doubt.
newsitem.headline: Liberia's Taylor stops campaign, poll date doubt.

text.p: Warlord Charles Taylor has halted his campaign for Liberia's presidency, bowing to a ban from the electoral commission which is discussing whether to postpone national elections scheduled for May 30.
Taylor said his decision to suspend the campaign, begun on Friday, followed a letter from the electoral commission about a ban on campaigning.
He made his position known in a radio broadcast on Monday.

Elections are pencilled in for May 30, but the head of the electoral commission has travelled to West African giant and power broker Nigeria to consult military ruler General Sani Abacha on a possible change of date.
Among the aspirants only Taylor, who plunged Liberia into civil war in 1989, favours the May election date.
Election officials say nine parties have registered for the ballot, part of a peace plan brokered by Liberia's neighbours and backed by their Nigerian-led West African peacekeeping force ECOMOG.
ECOMOG says it has gone a long way towards disarming the country's faction fighters.
The electoral commission, preparing for both legislative and presidential elections, still needs to recruit thousands of registrars for voting to take place.
Taylor's supporters took to the streets of the capital and parts of the interior last week, doling out election freebies -- tee-shirts, posters and stickers.
"We are obligated under the law to suspend the campaigning," said Arthur Massaquoi, public affairs officer of Taylor's National Patriotic Party (NPP).
Taylor's opponents include fellow faction leader Alhaji Kromah and U.N. Development Programme Africa director Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf.

The NPP's deputy national chairman, Christian Helbert, told a radio phone-in on Monday that trouble would follow if elections were delayed. He added that his partisans would resist the imposition of a new date.

The civil war, which has killed well over 150,000 people, began as an attempt by Taylor and his allies to drive coup-maker Master Sergeant Samuel Doe from power but disintegrated into a struggle for power among rival factions.

As many as one-half of Liberia's pre-war population of 2.5 million people have been displaced or have fled abroad. Several hundred thousand refugees are in neighbouring Ivory Coast, Guinea and Sierra Leone.
Liberia was founded by freed American slaves in 1847.
